# RustyNES v3.6.0 — "Octave"

The sixth release of the v3.1 to v4.0 line, on v3.5.1 "Reprise". The noise channel plays at its documented pitch, about an octave higher than every earlier release, in every game that uses it; NSF files play again; the MiSTer core runs PAL and Dendy consoles at full speed; and a source-level debugger for homebrew, audio stems, NSF ripping and libretro Core Options v2 arrive. **Movies and netplay peers from v3.5.1 are refused** (emulation epoch 8; v3.5.1 recorded 7), with a message naming both epochs. Desktop and libretro save states from v3.5.1 load. Netplay protocol 9 and `.rnm` format 7 are unchanged. MiSTer save states from v3.5.x are refused.

## Fixed

- **The noise channel plays at its documented pitch.** The NESdev page gives each noise period as the number of CPU cycles between shifts of the noise generator. RustyNES loaded that number into a timer that counts every other CPU cycle, so since v1.0.0 the noise shifted every 2 x (period + 1) CPU cycles: about half its rate, roughly an octave low, on every region. PAL's second period also read 7 where the page gives 8. Both are corrected in both cores, with a test of every period in both tables. Every game that uses the noise channel (drums, explosions, wind, footsteps) sounds different: 112 recorded audio checksums moved, and no picture or cycle count; 558 more, the coverage suite's checksums for local commercial dumps (the dumps themselves are not committed), moved the same way, each in its audio checksum alone. The defect was found by the MiSTer core's PAL work, whose ledger compares the two cores against the documentation: the oracle had the same convention, so no gate comparing the two could see it.
- **NSF files play again at the standard 60 Hz rate.** From v2.9.8 to v3.5.x an NSF's `play` routine never ran, so a tune played only what its `init` routine wrote (usually silence, or one held note). The player's driver enabled the vblank NMI inside the PPU's post-reset warm-up window, so the write was dropped, and it left the APU frame IRQ uninhibited, so the CPU spent the rest of the run servicing it. The driver now inhibits the frame IRQ before `init` and waits two vblanks before enabling the NMI, as nesdev's "NSF" and "PPU power up state" pages describe. 50 Hz and custom-rate NSFs were not affected.
- **MMC5 NSF files play.** The NSF driver's NMI entry sat at `$5015`, the MMC5's status port, and an NSF declaring MMC5 audio answers that port first, so the NMI ran the status byte as an instruction. The driver now sits at `$5100`, clear of every expansion chip an NSF can declare.

## How the noise fix was checked

- **No test ROM measures the noise pitch**, so the fix rests on the page, which states it three ways: the period "determines how many CPU cycles happen between shift register clocks"; its frequency table gives 447,443.2 Hz for NTSC index 0, which is 1,789,773 / 4 (the old code gave 178,977 Hz); and the APU page says the noise timer is clocked on every second CPU cycle and "thus produce[s] only even periods".
- **Measured against another emulator, as a black box.** A small test ROM holds the noise channel in its short (periodic) mode, so the output repeats and has a pitch. It was run through each libretro core with a minimal frontend, and the repeat was measured from the audio. At periods 7, 8, 10 and 12, RustyNES v3.6.0 and Nestopia both shift every 160, 202, 380 and 762 CPU cycles, the page's values; v3.5.1 shifted every 322, 406, 762 and 1,526. Mesen's libretro core crashed under that frontend and was not measured.
- **Not yet listened to.** The measurement checks the rate, not how real games sound; comparing a few games' drums and explosions against hardware or a trusted emulator is still to be done.

## Added

- **A source-level debugger for homebrew, `rustynes-dap`** (ADR 0049, `docs/dap-debugger.md`). A Debug Adapter Protocol server on stdio that an editor launches, reading cc65's `ld65 --dbgfile` output and the DWARF in llvm-mos's ELF: breakpoints on source lines, functions and addresses; `next`, `stepIn`, `stepOut`, instruction steps and `pause`; a call stack with each caller's line; parameters, locals, globals, registers, hover evaluation and `readMemory`. A stop adds no cycle, so a debugged machine equals the bare core byte for byte. With `--gdb 127.0.0.1:<port>` it is a GDB Remote Serial Protocol stub instead, loopback only. Neither protocol can write memory or registers. Tested with a scripted client against a cc65 and an llvm-mos build of a committed CC0 fixture, rebuilt from pinned toolchains by a new CI job; 14 mutants, all caught. Not yet tried: no released GDB or LLDB has a MOS target, so the stub has been driven only by the tests, and no VS Code extension ships. cc65 records no C types, so cc65 variables show as one byte.
- **Audio stems**: `rustynes stems <ROM>` writes pulse 1, pulse 2, triangle, noise, DMC and the cartridge's expansion chip as separate 32-bit float WAVs beside the console's mix, from one emulation pass. The 2A03 mixer is non-linear, so a seventh track carries the interaction term, and the seven sum to the mix (largest error 3.6e-7 over 650 frames of the VRC6 test ROM). Every run checks that its re-rendered mix equals the console's output bit for bit. See `docs/audio-stems.md`.
- **NSF ripping**: `rustynes nsf-rip <ROM>` traces a game, proposes its music driver's `play` and `init` routines with the evidence behind each, and with `--out` writes a version 1 NSF, plays it back, and reports it verified only when its `play` calls make the game's APU writes, call for call. Boards without PRG banking (mappers 0 and 3) only; anything else is refused with the reason.
- **libretro Core Options v2**: categories, a sublabel per option and a label per value, for frontends that ask for version 2 or more; older frontends get the same options as before, with the same keys and defaults.
- **More libretro options**: the CPU overclock (x1 to x4), the sprite limit, and the eight Vs. System DIP switches (each "Game default", Off or On), all three already on the desktop.
- **Float audio for libretro frontends that offer it** (`GET_AUDIO_SAMPLE_BATCH_FLOAT`, added to `libretro.h` in 2026): the mixer's samples are sent unconverted. Every other frontend, which today is every released one, gets the 16-bit stream byte for byte as before.
- **MiSTer core: PAL and Dendy consoles, at full speed.** A Region option in the OSD (Auto, NTSC, PAL, Dendy; Auto follows the image's header) selects the console. A 50 Hz console runs at its own 26.6017125 MHz master clock, with the SDRAM at exactly three times that, switched at run time through a reconfigurable PLL (ADR 0050). Without it a 50 Hz game would have run at 80.7 % speed. NTSC is unchanged bit for bit.

## Changed

- **libretro save states record the emulation options.** RetroArch replays movies from a state and starts a netplay peer from the host's state, so a state now carries the overclock, sprite limit, Four Score and forced DIP switches it was made under, and a restore applies them until a core option is changed. **States grow by 16 bytes.** States from earlier releases still load and leave the options alone.
- **Android targets Android 17 (API 37).** LAN and direct-IP netplay ask for the "Nearby devices" permission before hosting or joining, since Android 17 blocks local-network traffic otherwise; a refusal is explained, and room-code play is never asked. Audio is written without blocking and paced by the app. Checked on two Android 17 emulators; not yet on a device.
- **iOS saves are written durably**: every file the app writes is synced through the drive's cache before it replaces the old one, so a power loss cannot leave an empty save; and an FDS game's disk is written once a second, as on Android. The Swift has not been compiled for this release; the device checks are still to run.
- **The libretro core's Switch, PS Vita and 3DS builds are recorded as no-go**, with the checks that decided it (`docs/libretro/architecture.md`).

## Found, not fixed

- A Vs. DualSystem cabinet's save state does not round-trip byte for byte under the CPU overclock: 64 bytes of inert sprite-memory decay ages differ ten frames later. The game is unaffected, but a frontend comparing state checksums would see a desync. Pinned by an expected-fail probe.

## Provenance

- **A question for review, not a finding.** Before writing `rustynes-dap`'s cc65 reader, the agent that built it had read the desktop debugger's source-map module, which carries a Mesen2 `Provenance:` header. It wrote the new reader from ld65's own `--dbgfile` output and cc65's documentation, and put an origin disclosure at the top of the file rather than a `Provenance:` header. Whether that is a derivation needing a header, a provenance record and a `NOTICE` entry is the maintainer's judgement, not the tooling's; it is recorded here and in the v3.6.0 plan, and not certified either way.

## The MiSTer core

- **PAL and Dendy** as above, with every console and region table checked against the oracle's PAL and Dendy exports cycle for cycle, and the clock switch checked in simulation: the frame rate and a tone's pitch, timed against the programmed clock, are within 3e-9 of 60.0985 and 50.0070 Hz.
- **The noise fix** is in the RTL on both builds, with four new mutants of the old behaviour, all caught; its goldens come from this release's oracle.
- **Save states from v3.5.x are refused** on both builds: PAL and Dendy need a wider PPU counter, so the state is one bit longer and its layout fingerprint moved. An old state is refused for its header rather than misread.
- **The clocks pause during a region switch**, and the timing reports name the PLL's outputs `counter[N]`.
- **Not yet done:** a PAL entry in `yc.txt` for composite and S-video output.
- **New bitstreams** are compiled from the sibling's release commit at release time and attached here and to the sibling's release; their seed, checksums and timing margins are in its v3.6.0 notes.
- **Release candidate, not hardware-verified.** No hardware has run any bitstream; that the reconfigured PLL locks and the framework tolerates the paused clock can only be checked on a board.

## Verification

- The noise rule: a test of every period in both tables; 112 audio checksums re-recorded, and no frame or cycle count moved.
- The NSF fixes: each pinned by a test that counts `play` calls (`nsf_standard_rate_calls_play_every_frame` for the 60 Hz driver).
- The libretro options and the state record: C-ABI tests that drive the core as a frontend does.
- The release audits (anchors, state prose, notes rendering, the libretro `.info`, the contribution checklist) pass on the bumped tree.

## Install

- Download the pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows below.
- The MiSTer bitstreams are attached below as a release candidate, not hardware-verified: `RustyNES_MiSTer-v3.6.0.rbf` (off-die, needs SDRAM) and `RustyNES_MiSTer-v3.6.0-lite.rbf` (on-die).
- The WebAssembly build is live at [doublegate.github.io/RustyNES](https://doublegate.github.io/RustyNES/).
- The RetroArch core is in RetroArch's Online Updater on the platforms the libretro buildbot publishes to.
